title: The Midnight Crown
premise: In the city of Vellamare, where magic was outlawed after the gods fell silent, Dominic Almeida survives by hiding his gift for speaking with beasts behind a trade in harmless charms. When prayers begin to be answered again — first by animals, then by something older and hungrier wearing divine faces — Dominic discovers he is the last living heir of the beast-speakers who once sealed the covenant between realms. The old gods returning are not the merciful powers of legend but their corrupted remnants, feeding on stolen memories to rebuild themselves. To reforge the covenant, Dominic must gather a found family of outcasts, surrender his own most precious memories as payment, and at the climax choose between restoring his forgotten past or sealing the gate forever. He chooses the seal, losing every memory of the people who became his family — but they choose him again, telling him their story until love outlasts forgetting.
about_author: Hazel Quintana is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about quiet gifts, loud consequences, and the families we build from strangers.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: selling charms in Vellamare's night market while secretly bargaining with rats and gulls for information. A stray dog begs him for help, saying 'the door is open.' Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine; the first crack in five years of silence.

chapters.title: What the Gulls Remember
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: following the animals' warnings to a drowned shrine where a prayer is answered aloud — a fisherman's dead wife speaks back through the tide. Dominic flees, recognized by an inquisitor's hound. Beat: terror and longing intertwined; the past has teeth.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Hound
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Seraphine Vale, POV: she interrogates Dominic using her own bound beast-speaker gift, sensing his lie like a wrong note. She lets him go — deliberately — wanting him to lead her to the source. Beat: cat-and-mouse dread; mercy as a trap.

chapters.title: A Thief with Borrowed Eyes
chapters.summary: Nix, POV: a pickpocket who sees through animals' eyes when she sleeps robs Dominic, then returns everything, shaken — she dreamed his memories without permission. Beat: wary kinship; two hidden gifts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The God That Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: a neighborhood healer prays and receives a miracle that costs the whole street their recollection of one year. Dominic realizes the returned gods feed on memory. Beat: horror dawning; power given is never free.

chapters.title: The Last Bestiary
chapters.summary: Dominic and Nix, alternating: they find the ruined archive of the beast-speaker order and learn of the covenant — and that a seal requires a speaker willing to pay in memory. Beat: hope with a price tag; inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Brother Crow
chapters.summary: Crow (a corvid-speaker exiled from the order), POV: he tests Dominic cruelly, then teaches him the old tongue of beasts. First lesson: every word spoken to an animal is a promise. Beat: gruff mentorship; grief teaching discipline.

chapters.title: Seraphine's Empty Chapel
chapters.summary: Seraphine, POV: her faith curdles as she witnesses a god consume a congregation's names. She begins doubting the church she serves. Beat: disillusionment; the hunter questioning what she hunts for.

chapters.title: The Market Burns
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: inquisitors raid the night market hunting the 'beast-devil.' Nix is captured covering his escape. Beat: guilt and fury; found family forged in fire and failure.

chapters.title: Bargaining with Rats
chapters.summary: Dominic and Crow, POV shared: Dominic trades secrets with the city's rat-kings to locate Nix beneath the Inquisition. Beat: desperation and dark humor; small voices, big debts.

chapters.title: The Cells Below
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: rescue goes wrong; Seraphine corners him and he speaks to her hound, unbinding it. Freed, the hound chooses her over the church anyway. Beat: rupture and revelation; loyalty cannot be commanded.

chapters.title: An Inquisitor Defrocked
chapters.summary: Seraphine, POV: branded a heretic, she brings evidence of the memory-eating god to Dominic's group. Trust is negotiated, not given. Beat: uneasy alliance; enemies becoming something else.

chapters.title: Where the Old Gate Sleeps
chapters.summary: Crow, POV: the company journeys to the drowned covenant-gate beneath the sea-shrine, guided by creatures who remember the old world. Beat: pilgrimage wonder; the land itself as witness.

chapters.title: The God of Small Hungers
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: at the gate, a remnant god offers to restore his erased childhood if he opens the way fully. He nearly says yes. Beat: temptation; the sweetest lies are our own losses offered back.

chapters.title: Nix's Price
chapters.summary: Nix, POV: she learns the seal will take the caster's memories and volunteers instead, believing hers are worth least. Dominic refuses; they fight. Beat: heartbreak; self-worth as battlefield.

chapters.title: The Choir of Beasts
chapters.summary: All POVs braided: the gods converge on Vellamare, and every animal in the city turns to Dominic at once, offering their voices for the rite. Beat: awe and terror; the smallest creatures choosing sides.

chapters.title: Covenant, Broken and Remade
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: the rite begins at the gate. The remnant gods pour stolen memories at him like floodwater — including his mother's face, finally returned mid-casting. Beat: climax begins; drowning in what was taken.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: he can keep his restored past or spend it all to close the gate. He speaks the sealing words and lets himself forget — his childhood, his name's meaning, the people beside him. Beat: sacrifice; love measured in loss.

chapters.title: A Stranger in His Own Life
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: waking with hollow years, surrounded by strangers who weep at the sight of him. Seraphine, Nix, and Crow begin telling him who he was. Beat: disorientation and tenderness; identity as a story others hold for you.

chapters.title: Told Again
chapters.summary: Nix and Seraphine, alternating: over weeks they retell every chapter of their shared history. Animals confirm each detail; the dog from chapter one stays at his side. Beat: slow healing; memory rebuilt communally.

chapters.title: The New Covenant
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs: magic is legalized under a new accord written by speakers, thieves, and former inquisitors together. Dominic takes his place not as heir but as teacher. Beat: restoration; power shared instead of hoarded.

chapters.title: The Midnight Crown
chapters.summary: Dominic, POV: at the night market, now open and bright, a child asks why he wears a crown of woven feathers and bone charms. He answers honestly: because his friends crowned him with everything he can't remember. Beat: bittersweet peace; love that persists beyond memory.
